questions: Did the chest pain get worse with deep breathing or coughing (pleuritic pain), and can you point to a specific spot that reproduces the pain when pressed?
Do you have any fever, cough, or shortness of breath?
Did you have any recent injury to your chest, or do you have unequal breath sounds on one side (for example, one side feels “quieter” when you breathe)?
Do you have measured fever or did you take your temperature recently (even a low-grade fever)?
What is your current oxygen saturation (SpO₂) and heart rate, if you can measure them (or do you have any home pulse oximeter)?
Have you noticed any blue lips, fainting, or trouble speaking in full sentences because of shortness of breath?
When this pain and shortness of breath started, did the child have a recent episode of fast/shallow breathing, wheezing, or known exposure to smoke/allergens?
Does the child have any wheezing or noisy breathing (especially when exhaling) right now?
When you listen to his chest or when he speaks/breathes now, do you hear wheezing or noticeably reduced breath sounds on one side?
When you take a deep breath now, do you hear/feel wheezing (or has your asthma medicine, like albuterol, helped your breathing at all)?
answers: Yes—it's worse when I take a deep breath. I think it’s more on the right side, but I can feel it on both sides of my chest, and I can point to a spot that hurts more when you press it.
No fever and no cough. But I do feel short of breath/dyspnea quite a bit, and I feel lightheaded like I might faint.
No, I don’t have any chest injury. I don’t know if one side is quieter than the other, so I can’t say.
No—I haven’t measured my temperature, so I don’t know if I had any fever.
I don’t have a home pulse oximeter, so I can’t measure my oxygen saturation. I also don’t know my heart rate right now.
No blue lips. I haven’t fainted completely, but I feel like I’m about to. And I can speak in full sentences—I’m just really short of breath and scared.
I’ve had asthma before, and I’ve had to use a bronchodilator in the past, but I don’t remember wheezing right now. I don’t know about exposure to smoke or allergens.
I’m not sure—I don’t think it’s noisy wheezing, but I feel really tight and short of breath.
I can’t really tell what you would hear when you listen, and I don’t think one side is clearly reduced, but I’m not able to check that. I just feel tight and very short of breath.
I don’t hear wheezing myself. I don’t have albuterol with me right now, so I can’t say if it helped. Deep breaths still make the chest pain worse.
